_comment: FU-29 stage-2 baseline-and-no-regressions ratchet. This file documents the current state of all three quality tools (ruff, mypy, pytest-cov) and the CI floors that prevent regression. The ratchet strategy is: (1) the current measurement is the floor, (2) future BBFs that add new code must include tests that maintain or raise the floor, (3) the CI gate fails if the current measurement drops below the floor. See BBF-FU-29-stage-2-baseline-ratchet.md for the full strategy.

ruff.ci_command: ruff check libs services apps/cli tests scripts
ruff.ratchet_strategy: n/a (already at 0; any new finding fails the build)
ruff.notes: ruff is at 0 findings. Any new ruff finding is a CI failure. No ratchet needed.

mypy.ci_command: uv run mypy libs services apps/cli --no-incremental
mypy.ratchet_strategy: n/a (already at 0; any new error fails the build)
mypy.notes: mypy is at 0 errors with strict mode. Any new mypy error is a CI failure. No ratchet needed.

pytest-cov.ratchet_strategy: floor is 6% below baseline; raise the floor incrementally as new code is added with tests
pytest-cov.notes: Coverage is at 61% (4785 statements, 1711 missed, 1082 branches, 94 partial). The 55% floor is a 6% tolerance for natural variation in which tests are run on different platforms. When FU-20 and FU-21 land (A-F11 properties 2 and 3), 2 skipped tests will be enabled, potentially raising the baseline.

ratchet_rules.1_new_code_must_include_tests: Any new code (new files, new functions, new branches) must include tests that exercise the new code. The CI gate enforces this by failing the build if coverage drops below the floor.
ratchet_rules.2_floor_never_lowered: The current_floor for each tool MUST NEVER be lowered. If a tool's current_measurement drops below the floor, the build fails. The only way to lower the floor is to explicitly amend quality-ratchet.json with a justification.
ratchet_rules.3_measurement_must_stay_above_floor: The current_measurement for each tool MUST stay at or above the current_floor. If it drops, the build fails. The fix is to add tests for the uncovered code, not to lower the floor.
ratchet_rules.4_ignored_tests_documented: Any test that is skipped or ignored in the CI run MUST be documented in the tool's notes field with a justification (e.g., platform-specific, requires OS-level dependencies, blocked by an open FU).
